turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so I'll let you start, but I have a call at 4:40. My son found out he had a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and when?
An answer to what, Hale? You haven't asked me anything. I asked you who decided on the zero, and when.
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

"Admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM." I'm writing that down, Hale, word for word, and you haven't shown me one thing he'd be admitting to. Your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern and a first concern gets a supervised reassessment, so either you show me what you have right now, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.
Neither. My son doesn't sign a confession to something nobody has shown me, and the zero comes off. What do you have, Hale, or am I going upstairs?
